newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NNEC sees FY97/98 semiconductor profit up.
newsitem.headline: NNEC sees FY97/98 semiconductor profit up.

text.p: NEC Corp expected its profits from the semiconductor business to return to positive growth in fiscal 1997/98, rising by about 20 percent, Yuichi Haneta, executive vice president of NEC's LSI memory operations unit, said on Friday.
He said the company was investing US$0.9 billion in semiconductor production in fiscal 1996/97, out of NEC's total planned investment of US$1.9 billion in that period.
Haneta said NEC's semiconductor plant in Singapore would see a further investment of 4.0 billion yen in 1997.
Haneta was speaking to reporters at NEC Semiconductors Singapore Pte Ltd's 20th anniversary.
"Next year (fiscal 1997/98) I expect profit (from semiconductors) to increase by about 20 percent," said Haneta.
He said profit from semiconductors would see "several percent" decline in the the current fiscal year ending March 31 1997.
The expected fall in profit in current fiscal year was due to a decline in value of NEC's chip production as semiconductor prices sagged in 1996.
Haneta said he agreed with industry's estimates that the semiconductor market would grow by about 7.0 percent in 1997.
NEC would increase production of 64 MB dynamic random access memories (DRAMs) in 1997 where margins were better than 16 MB DRAMs, he said.

Haneta said the Singapore semiconductor plant would likely by the end of 1997, produce 500,000 pieces of 64 MB DRAMs per month, increasing its worldwide output of the memory chips to three million pieces per month by that time.

NEC would in 1997 invest another 4.0 billion yen in the Singapore plant which makes memory chips, ASIC (application specific integrated circuits) and memory modules, officials said. The plant currently produces about 6.0 million pieces of memory chips, mostly 16 MB DRAMs.
NEC has in the last 20 years invested about Singapore $500 million in the plant.
For the six months ended September 30 1996, NEC reported a net profit of about 31 billion yen, up from 15.5 billion yen in the previous period.
